arxiv-2107-06818.description: Abstract We present the results of the first calculation of the logarithmic corrections to the QCD contribution to same-sign W W -pair production, p ​ p → e ± ​ ν e ​ μ ± ​ ν μ ​ j ​ j pp\to e^{\pm}\nu_{e}\mu^{\pm}\nu_{\mu}jj , for same-sign charged leptons.

arxiv-2201-05663.title: Upward Lightning at the Gaisberg Tower: Initiation Mechanism and Flash Type and the Atmospheric Influence
arxiv-2201-05663.description: Abstract Upward lightning is much rarer than downward lightning and requires tall ( 100 + 100+ m) structures to initiate. It may be either triggered by other lightning discharges or completely self-initiated. While conventional lightning location systems reliably detect downward lightning, they miss a specific flash type of upward lightning that consists only of a continuous current.

arxiv-2211-00858.title: Conversation-oriented ASR with multi-look-ahead CBS architecture
arxiv-2211-00858.creator: Huaibo Zhao, Shinya Fujie, Tetsuji Ogawa, Jin Sakuma, Yusuke Kida*, Tetsunori Kobayashi
arxiv-2211-00858.description: Abstract During conversations, humans are capable of inferring the intention of the speaker at any point of the speech to prepare the following action promptly. Such ability is also the key for conversational systems to achieve rhythmic and natural conversation.

arxiv-2404-06445.title: Extremal minimal bipartite matching covered graphs
arxiv-2404-06445.creator: Amit Kumar Mallik, Ajit A. Diwan, Nishad Kothari
arxiv-2404-06445.description: Abstract A connected graph, on four or more vertices, is matching covered (aka 1 1 -extendable ) if every edge is present in some perfect matching. An ear decomposition theorem (similar to the one for 2 2 -connected graphs) exists for bipartite matching covered graphs due to Hetyei.

arxiv-2408-03969.title: GUP corrected Casimir Wormholes with Electric Charge in f ⁡ ( R , ℒ m ) f(R,\mathcal{L}_{m}) Gravity
arxiv-2408-03969.creator: Mohammed Muzakkir Rizwan, Zinnat Hassan, P.K. Sahoo
arxiv-2408-03969.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mohammed Muzakkir Rizwan, Zinnat Hassan, P.K. Sahoo. In this letter, we study and investigate the effects of the Generalised Uncertainty Principle (GUP) and electric charge on Casimir wormhole geometry in the Curvature-Lagrangian coupled f ⁡ ( R , ℒ m ) f(R,\mathcal{L}_{m}) gravity. The functional form of the considered model is f ⁡ ( R , ℒ m ) = R 2 ​ κ + ℒ m α f(R,\mathcal{L}_{m})=\frac{R}{2\kappa}+\mathcal{L}_{m}^{\,\,\alpha} , corresponding to it the analytic shape function is found.

arxiv-2501-13872.title: Global existence of Lagrangian solutions to the ionic Vlasov–Poisson system
arxiv-2501-13872.creator: Young-Pil Choi, Dowan Koo, Sihyun Song
arxiv-2501-13872.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Young-Pil Choi, Dowan Koo, Sihyun Song. In this paper, we study the Cauchy problem of the ionic Vlasov–Poisson (IVP) system for a broad class of initial data. To this end, we establish well-posedness and stability estimates for the Poisson–Boltzmann equation − Δ ​ Φ = ρ − e Φ -\Delta\Phi=\rho-e^{\Phi} provided ρ ∈ L + p \rho\in L_{+}^{p} with p > 1 p>1 , whereas previous approaches required p > d 2 p>\frac{d}{2} .

arxiv-2502-07658.description: Abstract . Most recommendation systems typically follow a product-based paradigm utilizing user-product interactions to identify the most engaging items for users. However, this product-based paradigm has notable drawbacks for Xianyu 1 1 1 Xianyu is China’s largest online C2C e-commerce platform where a large portion of the product are post by individual sellers .

arxiv-2504-00987.title: New Improvements in Solving Large LABS Instances Using Massively Parallelizable Memetic Tabu Search
arxiv-2504-00987.creator: Zhiwei Zhang, Jiayu Shen, Niraj Kumar, Marco Pistoia
arxiv-2504-00987.description: Abstract Low Autocorrelation Binary Sequences (LABS) is a particularly challenging binary optimization problem which quickly becomes intractable in finding the global optimum for problem sizes beyond 66. This aspect makes LABS appealing to use as a test-bed for meta-heuristic optimization solvers to target large problem sizes.

arxiv-2510-07484.creator: Haoyu Han, Kai Guo, Harry Shomer, Yu Wang, Yucheng Chu, Hang Li, Li Ma, Jiliang Tang
arxiv-2510-07484.description: Abstract . Reasoning over structured graphs remains a fundamental challenge for Large Language Models (LLMs), particularly when scaling to large graphs. Existing approaches typically follow the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) paradigm: first retrieving subgraphs relevant to the query and then generating answers conditioned on the retrieved subgraphs.

arxiv-2511-17848.title: Scaling Kinetic Monte-Carlo Simulations of Grain Growth with Combined Convolutional and Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2511-17848.creator: Zhihui Tian, Ethan Suwandi, Tomas Oppelstrup, Vasily V. Bulatov, Joel B. Harley, Fei Zhou
arxiv-2511-17848.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhihui Tian, Ethan Suwandi, Tomas Oppelstrup, Vasily V. Bulatov, Joel B. Harley, Fei Zhou. Graph neural networks (GNN) have emerged as a promising machine learning method for microstructure simulations such as grain growth. However, accurate modeling of realistic grain boundary networks requires large simulation cells, which GNN has difficulty scaling up to.

openalex-w3016939709.creator: Zuzana Kos, Elvire Roblin, Rim S. Kim, Stefan Michiels, Brandon D. Gallas, Weijie Chen, Koen K Van de Vijver, Shom Goel, Sylvia Adams, Sandra Demaria, Giuseppe Viale, Torsten O. Nielsen

Incorporating sTILs into clinical practice necessitates reproducible assessment. Previously developed standardized scoring

pmc-11389642.title: Association between serum calcium level and the risk of acute kidney injury in patients with acute myocardial infarction: evidences from the MIMIC-IV database
pmc-11389642.creator: Ya Wang, Yuli Lu, Chen Liu, Jiandong Xiao
pmc-11389642.description: ObjectiveThis cohort study was to assess the association between serum calcium levels and the risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients.MethodsThis study was analyzed using data of 1286 AMI patients aged ≥18 years who stayed in ICU more than 24 h in Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database.

pmc-11456737.title: Nerve Blocks for Post-Surgical Pain Management: A Narrative Review of Current Research
pmc-11456737.creator: Emery Niyonkuru, Muhammad Asad Iqbal, Rui Zeng, Xu Zhang, Peng Ma
pmc-11456737.description: Opioids remain the mainstay of post-surgical pain management; however, concerns regarding addiction and side effects necessitate the exploration of alternatives. This narrative review highlights the potential of nerve blocks as a safe and effective strategy for post-surgical pain control. This review explores the use of various nerve block techniques tailored to specific surgical procedures.

pmc-11571805.title: Regulatory interplay between SR proteins governs CLK1 kinase splice variants production
pmc-11571805.creator: Lulzim Shkreta, Aurélie Delannoy, Johanne Toutant, Benoit Chabot
pmc-11571805.description: The CLK1 kinase phosphorylates SR proteins to modulate their splicing regulatory activity. Skipping of alternative exon 4 on the CLK1 pre-mRNA produces a CLK1 variant lacking the catalytic site. Here, we aimed to understand how various SR proteins integrate into the regulatory program that controls CLK1 exon 4 splicing.

pmc-11697996.title: Component Mix-Match for Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty Revision: A Case Report
pmc-11697996.creator: Ilias Tsolis, Fady Atia, Malin Wijeratna
pmc-11697996.description: Although mixing and matching components is a common, safe, and well-documented practice in hip revision surgery, our extensive search indicates that it has not been previously reported for shoulder arthroplasty. This case report presents the use of mixed implants in shoulder revision surgery to reduce morbidity and address flaws in the initial implant design.

pmc-12711886.title: Changes in microbiota associated with the use of intragastric balloons
pmc-12711886.creator: Natalia Komorniak, Danuta Cembrowska-Lech, Anna Wiechowska-Kozłowska, Katarzyna Gaweł, Jan Pawlus, Karolina Skonieczna-Żydecka, Tadeusz Sulikowski, Alexandra Martynova van Kley, Ewa Stachowska
pmc-12711886.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Obesity is a chronic disease characterized by excessive accumulation of adipose tissue. Intragastric balloon (IGB) implantation is one of the methods used to treat obesity. The aim of the study was to investigate whether the composition of the balloon-associated microbiota changes based on the duration of implantation and whether there is an association between changes in microbiota and weight loss results. In patients who lost weight, the microbial community was more diverse.

pmc-12785036.title: Transformer-Based Classification of Transposable Element Consensus Sequences with TEclass2
pmc-12785036.creator: Lucas Bickmann, Matias Rodriguez, Xiaoyi Jiang, Wojciech Makałowski
pmc-12785036.description: Simple SummaryTransposable elements (TEs) are mobile genetic elements that are present in great numbers in the majority of eukaryotic genomes. They are major drivers of genome evolution as they can facilitate chromosome rearrangements, provide mechanisms for genomic shuffling, and contribute to genome expansion, thereby altering genome architecture.

pmc-13083935.title: Association between stress hyperglycemia ratio and all-cause mortality in neurocritical patients
pmc-13083935.creator: Yuyang Pan, Wen Tan, Jianhua Peng, Kuangyang Yu, Yubin Yang, Jinwei Pang, Yong Jiang
pmc-13083935.description: Fluctuations in blood glucose during acute neurocritical illness are associated with poor outcomes, but the role of stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) in predicting outcomes across diverse neurocritical conditions remains unclear. This study evaluated SHR as a prognostic indicator for short and long-term mortality and its utility in machine learning-enhanced predictive models.

pmc-13221519.title: Socioemotional factors associated with teacher resilience in Colombian communities affected by armed conflict a cross-sectional study
pmc-13221519.creator: Lina María González-Ballesteros, Camila Andrea Castellanos-Roncancio, Oscar Eduardo Gómez Cardenas, Jennifer Clavijo-Marín, Luis Eduardo Mojica Ospina, Luis Alberto López-Romero
pmc-13221519.description: IntroductionMental health problems are increasingly prevalent among school-aged children and adolescents, underscoring the need for teacher-inclusive mental health interventions.ObjectivesTo examine the association between sociodemographic and socioemotional factors and resilience among teachers, prior to their participation in a school-based intervention aimed at strengthening socioemotional competencies.

pmc-13264101.title: Cortical transcriptomic dysregulation in Autism spectrum disorder: A conceptual synthesis
pmc-13264101.creator: Ruslan Kurmashev
pmc-13264101.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition in which human post-mortem cortical transcriptomic studies have identified recurrent but context-sensitive molecular abnormalities. This narrative review synthesises RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) evidence from ASD cortex and organises recurrent findings into three interacting cortical domains: synaptic/neuronal programmes, immune-glial programmes, and RNA-regulatory processes.

pmc-13301099.title: The impact of mitigating perioperative inflammation on risk of conduction disturbances after transcatheter aortic valve implantation; is it time to coat the valve?
pmc-13301099.creator: K Abdelsayed, A M Amin, M C Downey, A Almahdy, M T Desouki, D Witt, E Zishiri, J Sengupta
pmc-13301099.description: IntroductionPostoperative conduction disturbances, partially mediated by procedural inflammation and edema, represent a significant challenge after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). They are associated with higher morbidity and mortality, especially in patients at high risk of conduction disturbances. It is unclear whether mitigating the local inflammation around the valve perioperatively can reduce the risk of these complications.

pmc-13346559.title: PS-10 - MASS CASUALTY PLANS FOR A RESILIENT HEALTH AND SOCIAL CARE SYSTEM: WHAT RISKS AND IMPACTS DO PLANNERS CONSIDER
pmc-13346559.creator: Dr Padraig Lyons, Professor Kate Cochrane
pmc-13346559.description: BackgroundMass casualty incidents (MCIs) such as major accidents, fires, or other natural disasters present multifaceted challenges that can rapidly overwhelm health and social care systems. Existing service pressures within health and social care services raise concerns about the adaptability and sustainability of current mass casualty planning approaches, including how recovery is addressed.

pmc-13474748.title: Acute kidney injury among intensive care unit patients in Denmark: temporal changes in mortality and kidney outcomes from 2010 to 2024

pmc-13592844.title: Benefits and risks of consuming Cannabis sativa L. in food
pmc-13592844.creator: Ewa Matyjaszczyk, Maria Śmiechowska
pmc-13592844.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). or hemp is a cosmopolitan, multi-purpose plant and area of its cultivation has been growing in recent years. Its public perception is influenced by potential to produce narcotic substances. However, hemp seed can be a valuable source of nutrients for humans and may be of particular interest in more sustainable food consumption patterns, including vegetarian and flexitarian diets. The paper presents benefits and risks of hemp seeds in case of their consumption in food. Low cannabinoids varieties are considered only.

pmc-13658865.title: A new era in computational pathology: A survey on foundation and vision-language models
pmc-13658865.creator: Dibaloke Chanda, Milan Aryal, Masoud Ganji, Anil Parwani, Nasim Yahya Soltani
pmc-13658865.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Recent advances in deep learning have completely transformed the domain of computational pathology (CPath). More specifically, it has altered the diagnostic workflow of pathologists by integrating foundation models (FMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) in their assessment and decision-making process. The limitations of existing deep learning approaches in CPath can be overcome by FMs through learning a representation space that can be adapted to a wide variety of downstream tasks without explicit supervision.
